challenge.title: Viewing a flat
challenge.instructions: Write a short conversation in Fusha in which you ask about a flat for rent, its bedrooms, floor and monthly rent, ask to see it, ask whether it is furnished, find the kitchen, and say what you will take.
required_elements: a question about the rent or the number of bedrooms using كَمْ
a question about the floor, the lift or whether water and electricity are included
a request to see the flat using هَلْ أَسْتَطِيعُ
a question about the kitchen or the furniture using أَيْنَ or هَلْ
a closing decision with سَآخُذُهَا or أُرِيدُ عَقْدَ إِيجَارٍ

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. أَبْحَثُ عَنْ شَقَّةٍ لِلْإِيجَار. كَمِ الْإِيجَارُ الشَّهْرِيّ؟
dialogue.transliteration: as-salaamu 3alaykum. abHathu 3an shaqqatin lil-iijaar. kami al-iijaaru ash-shahriyy?
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you. I am looking for a flat to rent. How much is the monthly rent?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَام. أَلْفُ دِينَارٍ فِي الشَّهْر، وَفِيهَا ثَلَاثُ غُرَفِ نَوْم.
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3alaykumu as-salaam. alfu deenaarin fii ash-shahr, wa feehaa thalaathu ghurafi nawm.
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you. A thousand dinars a month, and it has three bedrooms.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: فِي أَيِّ طَابِقٍ؟ وَهَلْ يُوجَدُ مِصْعَدٌ؟
dialogue.transliteration: fii ayyi Taabiqin? wa hal yoojadu miS3ad?
dialogue.english: Which floor? And is there a lift?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: فِي الطَّابِقِ الثَّانِي، وَفِي الْمَبْنَى مِصْعَد.
dialogue.transliteration: fii aT-Taabiqi ath-thaanee, wa fii al-mabnaa miS3ad.
dialogue.english: On the second floor, and the building has a lift.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: هَلْ أَسْتَطِيعُ مُعَايَنَةَ الشَّقَّة؟ وَهَلْ هِيَ مَفْرُوشَة؟
dialogue.transliteration: hal astaTee3u mu3aayanata ash-shaqqa? wa hal hiya mafroosha?
dialogue.english: Can I view the flat? And is it furnished?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: تَفَضَّلْ. فِيهَا أَثَاثٌ كَامِل، وَالْمَطْبَخُ بِجَانِبِ غُرْفَةِ الْجُلُوس.
dialogue.transliteration: tafaDDal. feehaa athaathun kaamil, wa al-maTbakhu bijaanibi ghurfati al-juloos.
dialogue.english: Please come in. It has full furniture, and the kitchen is next to the living room.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: جَمِيلَة. سَآخُذُهَا، وَأُرِيدُ عَقْدَ إِيجَارٍ لِسَنَة.
dialogue.transliteration: jameela. saakhudhuhaa, wa ureedu 3aqda iijaarin li-sana.
dialogue.english: Lovely. I will take it, and I want a one-year lease.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: حَسَنًا. جَزَاكَ اللهُ خَيْرًا.
dialogue.transliteration: Hasanan. jazaaka Allaahu khayran.
dialogue.english: Good. May Allah reward you with good.

reply.english: Yes, the building has a lift.
From the first of the month.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. أَبْحَثُ عَنْ شَقَّةٍ لِلْإِيجَار.
dialogue.transliteration: as-salaamu 3alaykum. abHathu 3an shaqqatin lil-iijaar.
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you. I am looking for a flat to rent.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَام. عِنْدِي شَقَّةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ قَرِيبَةٌ مِنَ الْمَسْجِد.
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3alaykumu as-salaam. 3indee shaqqatun jameelatun qareebatun mina al-masjid.
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you. I have a lovely flat near the masjid.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: كَمْ غُرْفَةَ نَوْمٍ فِيهَا؟
dialogue.transliteration: kam ghurfata nawmin feehaa?
dialogue.english: How many bedrooms does it have?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: ثَلَاثُ غُرَفِ نَوْمٍ، وَهِيَ فِي الطَّابِقِ الثَّانِي.
dialogue.transliteration: thalaathu ghurafi nawmin, wa hiya fii aT-Taabiqi ath-thaanee.
dialogue.english: Three bedrooms, and it is on the second floor.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: هَلْ يُوجَدُ مِصْعَدٌ؟
dialogue.transliteration: hal yoojadu miS3ad?
dialogue.english: Is there a lift?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، فِي الْمَبْنَى مِصْعَد.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, fii al-mabnaa miS3ad.
dialogue.english: Yes, the building has a lift.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: كَمِ الْإِيجَارُ الشَّهْرِيّ؟
dialogue.transliteration: kami al-iijaaru ash-shahriyy?
dialogue.english: How much is the monthly rent?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: أَلْفُ دِينَارٍ فِي الشَّهْر، وَالْمَاءُ وَالْكَهْرَبَاءُ عَلَيْك.
dialogue.transliteration: alfu deenaarin fii ash-shahr, wa al-maa2u wal-kahrabaa2u 3alayk.
dialogue.english: A thousand dinars a month, and water and electricity are on you.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: هَلْ أَسْتَطِيعُ مُعَايَنَةَ الشَّقَّةِ الْيَوْم؟
dialogue.transliteration: hal astaTee3u mu3aayanata ash-shaqqati al-yawm?
dialogue.english: Can I view the flat today?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: بِالتَّأْكِيد. تَفَضَّلْ، هَذِهِ مَفَاتِيحُ الشَّقَّة.
dialogue.transliteration: bit-ta2keed. tafaDDal, hadhihi mafaateeHu ash-shaqqa.
dialogue.english: Of course. Please, here are the keys to the flat.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: الشَّقَّةُ مُنَاسِبَة، سَآخُذُهَا. أُرِيدُ عَقْدَ إِيجَارٍ لِسَنَة.
dialogue.transliteration: ash-shaqqatu munaasiba, saakhudhuhaa. ureedu 3aqda iijaarin li-sana.
dialogue.english: The flat is suitable, I will take it. I want a one-year lease.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: حَسَنًا. تَدْفَعُ إِيجَارَ شَهْرٍ تَأْمِينًا، وَتَنْتَقِلُ أَوَّلَ الشَّهْر.
dialogue.transliteration: Hasanan. tadfa3u iijaara shahrin ta2meenan, wa tantaqilu awwala ash-shahr.
dialogue.english: Good. You pay one month's rent as a deposit, and you move in on the first of the month.

pair.english: How much is the monthly rent?
How many bedrooms does it have?

response.english: Yes, the building has a lift.

lessons.culture: In many Arab cities rent is quoted per month, and a deposit of about one month's rent is common. Flats are often described by their rooms, so ask whether the living room is counted. Always ask whether water and electricity are included, and sign a written lease before paying anything.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'How many bedrooms does it have?'
exercises.tip: kam asks how many; the counted noun after it is singular and takes fatha.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I want a one-year lease'
exercises.tip: 3aqd is a contract; iijaar is renting; li-sana is for a year.

exercises.prompt: Which one means 'Is there a lift?'
exercises.tip: yoojadu means there is; miS3ad is a lift.

exercises.prompt: Which one means 'How much is the monthly rent?'
exercises.tip: kam is how much; shahriyy means monthly.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'I am looking for a flat to rent'
exercises.tip: baHatha 3an means to search for; lil-iijaar means for rent.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'It is on the second floor'
exercises.tip: Taabiq is a floor; ath-thaanee is the second.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'كَمْ _____ نَوْمٍ فِيهَا؟' (How many bedrooms does it have?)
exercises.tip: ghurfa is a room; after kam it is singular with fatha.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'هَذِهِ _____ الشَّقَّة' (Here are the keys of the flat)
exercises.tip: mafaateeH is keys; it drops its tanween before the next noun.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'كَمِ الْإِيجَارُ الشَّهْرِيّ؟'. Say: a thousand dinars a month.
exercises.tip: alf is a thousand; fii ash-shahr is in the month.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'هَلْ يُوجَدُ مِصْعَدٌ؟'. Say: yes, the building has a lift.
exercises.tip: al-mabnaa is the building.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: تَفَضَّلْ، هَذِهِ غُرْفَةُ الْجُلُوس.
dialogue.transliteration: tafaDDal, hadhihi ghurfatu al-juloos.
dialogue.english: Please come in, this is the living room.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: مَا شَاءَ اللهُ، وَاسِعَة. هَلِ الشَّقَّةُ مَفْرُوشَة؟
dialogue.transliteration: maa shaa2a Allaah, waasi3a. hali ash-shaqqatu mafroosha?
dialogue.english: Mashallah, it is spacious. Is the flat furnished?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، فِيهَا أَثَاثٌ كَامِل. فِي غُرْفَةِ الْجُلُوسِ أَرِيكَةٌ وَطَاوِلَة.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, feehaa athaathun kaamil. fii ghurfati al-juloosi areekatun wa Taawila.
dialogue.english: Yes, it has full furniture. The living room has a sofa and a table.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: وَأَيْنَ الْمَطْبَخ؟
dialogue.transliteration: wa ayna al-maTbakh?
dialogue.english: And where is the kitchen?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: بِجَانِبِ غُرْفَةِ الْجُلُوس. وَالثَّلَّاجَةُ عِنْدَ الْبَاب.
dialogue.transliteration: bijaanibi ghurfati al-juloos. wa ath-thallaajatu 3inda al-baab.
dialogue.english: Next to the living room. And the fridge is at the door.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: هَلِ الْمُكَيِّفُ يَعْمَل؟
dialogue.transliteration: hali al-mukayyifu ya3mal?
dialogue.english: Does the air conditioner work?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، يَعْمَلُ جَيِّدًا. وَهَذِهِ غُرْفَةُ النَّوْم.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, ya3malu jayyidan. wa hadhihi ghurfatu an-nawm.
dialogue.english: Yes, it works well. And this is the bedroom.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: غُرْفَةُ النَّوْمِ وَاسِعَة، لَكِنِّي أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى سَرِيرٍ جَدِيد.
dialogue.transliteration: ghurfatu an-nawmi waasi3a, lakinnee aHtaaju ilaa sareerin jadeed.
dialogue.english: The bedroom is spacious, but I need a new bed.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: لَا مُشْكِلَة. وَهُنَاكَ خِزَانَةٌ لِلْمَلَابِس.
dialogue.transliteration: laa mushkila. wa hunaaka khizaanatun lil-malaabis.
dialogue.english: No problem. And there is a wardrobe for clothes.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: كَمْ حَمَّامًا فِي الشَّقَّة؟
dialogue.transliteration: kam Hammaaman fii ash-shaqqa?
dialogue.english: How many bathrooms are in the flat?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: حَمَّامَانِ. لَكِنَّ مِصْبَاحَ الْمَمَرِّ لَا يَعْمَل.
dialogue.transliteration: Hammaamaan. lakinna miSbaaHa al-mamarri laa ya3mal.
dialogue.english: Two bathrooms. But the hallway light does not work.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: لَا بَأْسَ، أَصْلِحْهُ مِنْ فَضْلِك وَأَنَا آخُذُ الشَّقَّة.
dialogue.transliteration: laa ba2s, aSliHhu min faDlik wa anaa aakhudhu ash-shaqqa.
dialogue.english: No worries, please fix it and I will take the flat.

pair.english: How many bathrooms are in the flat?
Where do I put the fridge?

lessons.culture: A flat is often described by its rooms: the majlis or living room, the bedrooms, the kitchen and the bathrooms. In many Gulf homes the majlis is a separate room for guests. A flat may be rented furnished or empty, so ask exactly what stays, such as the fridge, the wardrobes and the air conditioners.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Where is the kitchen?'
exercises.tip: ayna asks where; maTbakh is the place of cooking.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Is the flat furnished?'
exercises.tip: hal opens a yes-or-no question; mafroosha comes from farasha, to furnish.

exercises.prompt: Which one means 'There is a sofa in the living room'?
exercises.tip: areeka is a sofa; fii ghurfati al-juloos is in the living room.

exercises.prompt: Which one means 'How many bathrooms are in the flat?'
exercises.tip: Hammaam is a bathroom; after kam it is singular with fatha.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'Put the table here'
exercises.tip: Da3 is the command put; hunaa is here.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'The bedroom is spacious'
exercises.tip: waasi3a describes the room and agrees with it.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'أَيْنَ _____ الْمَلَابِس؟' (Where is the wardrobe?)
exercises.tip: khizaana is a cupboard; here it is the first word of a two-word phrase.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'هَلِ _____ يَعْمَل؟' (Does the air conditioner work?)
exercises.tip: mukayyif is an air conditioner; ya3mal means works.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'أَيْنَ الْمَطْبَخ؟'. Say: next to the living room.
exercises.tip: bijaanib means beside.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'كَمْ حَمَّامًا فِي الشَّقَّة؟'. Say: two bathrooms.
exercises.tip: The dual ending -aani means exactly two.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا يُوسُف. الصُّنْبُورُ يُسَرِّبُ الْمَاء، هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ إِصْلَاحَهُ؟
dialogue.transliteration: as-salaamu 3alayka yaa yoosuf. aS-Sunbuuru yusarribu al-maa2, hal tastaTee3u iSlaaHahu?
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you, Yusuf. The tap is leaking water, can you fix it?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكَ السَّلَام. نَعَمْ، سَأُحَاوِل. أَيْنَ صُنْدُوقُ الْعُدَّة؟
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3alayka as-salaam. na3am, sa-uHaawil. ayna Sunduuqu al-3udda?
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you. Yes, I will try. Where is the toolbox?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: فِي الْمَخْزَن. تَفَضَّل.
dialogue.transliteration: fee al-makhzan. tafaDDal.
dialogue.english: In the storeroom. Please.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: نَاوِلْنِي الْمِفَكّ. وَأَحْتَاجُ إِلَى مِطْرَقَةٍ وَمَسَامِير.
dialogue.transliteration: naawilnee al-mifakk. wa aHtaaju ilaa miTraqatin wa masaameer.
dialogue.english: Pass me the screwdriver. And I need a hammer and nails.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: حَاضِر. وَالْبَابُ لَا يُغْلَقُ جَيِّدًا أَيْضًا.
dialogue.transliteration: HaaDir. wa al-baabu laa yughlaqu jayyidan aydan.
dialogue.english: Right away. And the door does not close well either.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: سَأَنْظُرُ فِيهِ بَعْدَ قَلِيل. هَلِ الْكَهْرَبَاءُ مَقْطُوعَةٌ فِي الْبَيْت؟
dialogue.transliteration: sa-anZuru feehi ba3da qaleel. hali al-kahrabaa2u maqToo3atun fee al-bayt?
dialogue.english: I will look at it shortly. Is the power out in the house?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: لَا، لَكِنَّ الْمِصْبَاحَ لَا يَعْمَل.
dialogue.transliteration: laa, lakinna al-miSbaaHa laa ya3mal.
dialogue.english: No, but the light bulb does not work.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: غَيِّرِ الْمِصْبَاحَ أَوَّلًا. وَاتَّصِلْ بِالسَّبَّاكِ إِنْ لَزِم.
dialogue.transliteration: ghayyiri al-miSbaaHa awwalan. wa ittaSil bi-s-sabbaaki in lazim.
dialogue.english: Change the bulb first. And call the plumber if needed.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: كَمِ التَّكْلِفَةُ إِنْ جَاءَ السَّبَّاك؟
dialogue.transliteration: kami at-takleefatu in jaa2a as-sabbaak?
dialogue.english: How much is the cost if the plumber comes?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: أَظُنُّهَا قَلِيلَة. اِنْتَهَيْتُ، جَرِّبِ الصُّنْبُور.
dialogue.transliteration: aDhunnuhaa qaleela. intahaytu, jarribi aS-Sunbuur.
dialogue.english: I think it is small. I have finished, try the tap.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: شُكْرًا، إِنَّهُ يَعْمَلُ الْآن.
dialogue.transliteration: shukran, innahu ya3malu al-aan.
dialogue.english: Thanks, it works now.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه. جَزَاكَ اللَّهُ خَيْرًا.
dialogue.transliteration: al-Hamdu lillaah. jazaaka Allaahu khayran.
dialogue.english: Praise be to Allah. May Allah reward you with good.

lessons.culture: A home repair is often a favour between brothers, relatives or neighbours before anyone is paid, and the helper is thanked with جَزَاكَ اللَّهُ خَيْرًا. People say الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه when a job ends well and إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه when they promise to try. A professional such as a plumber or electrician is called when the problem is beyond a simple fix, and it is polite to ask the cost before the work starts.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'The tap is leaking water'
exercises.tip: yusarribu means leaks; Sunbuur is a tap.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Where is the toolbox?'
exercises.tip: 3udda means tools, a set of equipment.

exercises.prompt: Which one means 'Pass me the screwdriver'?
exercises.tip: naawil means hand over.

exercises.prompt: Which one means 'The power is out in the house'?
exercises.tip: maqToo3a means cut off.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'I need a hammer and nails'
exercises.tip: aHtaaju is followed by ilaa.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'The door does not close well'
exercises.tip: laa before the verb makes it negative.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'الْبَابُ لَا _____ جَيِّدًا' (The door does not close well)
exercises.tip: yughlaqu is passive: it is not closed.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'اِتَّصِلْ بِ_____ إِنْ لَزِم' (Call the plumber if needed)
exercises.tip: sabbaak is a plumber; after bi- it ends in -i.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ إِصْلَاحَهُ؟'. Say: Yes, I will try.
exercises.tip: sa- before a verb makes it future.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'شُكْرًا، إِنَّهُ يَعْمَلُ الْآن'. Reply.
exercises.tip: Praise Allah when a job ends well.

reply.english: May Allah reward you with good.
In the bin at the entrance.

reply.arabic: إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه، فِي وَقْتٍ آخَر
reply.transliteration: in shaa2a Allaah, fee waqtin aakhar

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. نَحْنُ جِيرَانُكُمُ الْجُدُد.
dialogue.transliteration: as-salaamu 3alaykum. naHnu jeeraanukumu al-judud.
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you. We are your new neighbours.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَام. أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا بِكُمْ. فِي أَيِّ شَقَّةٍ تَسْكُن؟
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3alaykumu as-salaam. ahlan wa sahlan bikum. fee ayyi shaqqatin taskun?
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you. Welcome. Which flat do you live in?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: نَسْكُنُ فِي الشَّقَّةِ الْمُجَاوِرَة، فِي الطَّابِقِ الثَّالِث.
dialogue.transliteration: naskunu fee ash-shaqqati al-mujaawira, fee aT-Taabiqi ath-thaalith.
dialogue.english: We live in the flat next door, on the third floor.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: أَحْضَرْتُ لَكُمْ بَعْضَ الطَّعَام.
dialogue.transliteration: aHDartu lakum ba3Da aT-Ta3aam.
dialogue.english: I brought you some food.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: جَزَاكَ اللَّهُ خَيْرًا. هَلْ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَسْتَعِيرَ سُلَّمًا؟
dialogue.transliteration: jazaaka Allaahu khayran. hal astaTee3u an astaa3eera sullaman?
dialogue.english: May Allah reward you with good. May I borrow a ladder?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: طَبْعًا، تَفَضَّلْ. وَتَعَالَ اشْرَبِ الشَّايَ مَعَنَا.
dialogue.transliteration: Tab3an, tafaDDal. wa ta3aala ishrabi ash-shaaya ma3anaa.
dialogue.english: Of course, please. And come and have tea with us.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه، فِي وَقْتٍ آخَر. أَيْنَ نَضَعُ النُّفَايَات؟
dialogue.transliteration: in shaa2a Allaah, fee waqtin aakhar. ayna naDa3u an-nufaayaat?
dialogue.english: If Allah wills, another time. Where do we put the rubbish?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: فِي الْحَاوِيَةِ عِنْدَ الْمَدْخَل. وَهَلْ تُحَرِّكُ سَيَّارَتَكَ مِنْ فَضْلِك؟
dialogue.transliteration: fee al-Haawiyati 3inda al-madkhal. wa hal tuHarriku sayyaarataka min faDlik?
dialogue.english: In the bin at the entrance. And could you move your car, please?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: حَاضِر، أَعْتَذِرُ عَنِ الْإِزْعَاج.
dialogue.transliteration: HaaDir, a3tadhiru 3ani al-iz3aaj.
dialogue.english: Right away, I apologise for the disturbance.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: لَا عَلَيْك. جَارُنَا مَرِيض، سَنَزُورُهُ غَدًا.
dialogue.transliteration: laa 3alayk. jaarunaa mareeD, sa-nazooruhu ghadan.
dialogue.english: Not at all. Our neighbour is ill, we will visit him tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: لِلْجَارِ حَقٌّ عَلَيْنَا. هَلْ تَسْتَلِمُ بَرِيدَنَا أَثْنَاءَ سَفَرِنَا؟
dialogue.transliteration: lil-jaari Haqqun 3alaynaa. hal tastalimu bareedanaa athnaa2a safarinaa?
dialogue.english: A neighbour has a right over us. Will you receive our mail while we travel?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: بِكُلِّ سُرُور. بَارَكَ اللَّهُ فِيكُم.
dialogue.transliteration: bi-kulli suroor. baaraka Allaahu feekum.
dialogue.english: With pleasure. May Allah bless you.

pair.english: Which flat do you live in?
Where do we put the rubbish?

response.english: In the bin at the entrance.

lessons.culture: In Islam a neighbour has a great right. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said that Jibril kept advising him about the neighbour until he thought the neighbour would be made an heir. Neighbours share food, visit one another when ill, keep an eye on each other's homes and avoid disturbing each other with noise. Sending a dish to the new family next door is a common way to start a friendship.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'We are your new neighbours'
exercises.tip: jeeraan is neighbours, the plural of jaar.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Where do we put the rubbish?'
exercises.tip: nufaayaat is rubbish, always plural.

exercises.prompt: Which one means 'I brought you some food'?
exercises.tip: ba3D means some of.

exercises.prompt: Which one means 'A neighbour has a right over us'?
exercises.tip: li- plus a noun shows ownership: the neighbour has a right.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'Which flat do you live in?'
exercises.tip: ayy means which and comes after the preposition.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'Could you move your car, please?'
exercises.tip: hal opens a yes-or-no question.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'هَلْ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَسْتَعِيرَ _____؟' (May I borrow a ladder?)
exercises.tip: sullam is a ladder; as the object it takes -an.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'أَحْضَرْتُ لَكُمْ بَعْضَ _____' (I brought you some food)
exercises.tip: Ta3aam is food.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'أَحْضَرْتُ لَكُمْ بَعْضَ الطَّعَام'. Reply.
exercises.tip: Thank a gift with jazaaka Allaahu khayran.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'تَعَالَ اشْرَبِ الشَّايَ مَعَنَا'. Say: If Allah wills, another time.
exercises.answer: إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه، فِي وَقْتٍ آخَر

in shaa2a Allaah, fee waqtin aakhar
exercises.tip: A polite way to postpone an invitation.
